resources.string: Wireless debugging, one QR away. Get your phone ready, then let your terminal do the rest.
Use the same network as your computer.
Tap Build number 7 times in About phone.
Next, turn on Wireless debugging in Settings.
Run easyadb to display a fresh pairing QR.
In Developer options, turn on Wireless debugging and allow your Wi-Fi network.
Tap Pair device with QR code in Wireless debugging. Scan the terminal QR with that scanner.
Then choose Wireless debugging → Pair device with QR code.
Android handles the scan and pairing in Settings. EasyADB guides setup; the terminal confirms when your phone is connected.
Shortcut added. Swipe down to find EasyADB.
Swipe down, edit your Quick Settings tiles, and drag EasyADB into the panel.

The QR must be scanned from Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with QR code, not your regular camera.

Nothing appearing? Keep both devices on the same Wi-Fi. VPNs, guest networks, and firewalls can block discovery. On your computer, run easyadb doctor.

Pair manually: choose Pair device with pairing code in Settings. On your computer run:

easyadb pair IP:PAIRING_PORT

Enter the six-digit code at the hidden prompt. If needed, run:

easyadb connect IP:CONNECTION_PORT

The connection port is on the main Wireless debugging page; it differs from the pairing port.

To remove a computer’s access, tap its name under Paired devices in Settings and choose Forget.
Open your phone’s Settings manually, then find Developer options.
